claims.plain_claim: In transfer mode the x402 server verifies an SPL token payment on-chain before serving the resource.
authority_assumptions: The seller trusts its configured Solana RPC endpoint to report transaction status and balances.
claims.test_command: npm --prefix x402 ci --ignore-scripts && npm --prefix x402 run build && npm --prefix x402 test

test_run.environment: node:22 container, network off, sources from git archive of 8743fd7
test_run.note: 1565 passed, 8 skipped, 3 failed of 1576: repo-identity needs git and two polyglot tests need python3 and cargo, none installed in the container

mocks_or_skips: Unit tests use mocked RPC responses; no devnet transfer was executed in this pass.
demonstrated_properties: transaction must exist without error at the configured commitment (default confirmed; finalized can be required)
recipient balance increase for the quoted mint must cover the quote total
payment proof older than 900 s is refused
a reused proof is refused within one running process
not_demonstrated: replay rejection across restarts or instances (ReplayStore is an in-process Map even when a database URL is set)
binding of the payment to the quote nonce unless REQUIRE_PAYMENT_MEMO is enabled (off by default)
binding of the transaction sender to the buyer
native SOL payments
operational_limitations: npm latest 0.1.1 is deprecated; Git 0.2.0 is not on npm, so install from source until it is published.

claims.plain_claim: Every paid response carries an Ed25519-signed receipt that links to the previous receipt hash.
authority_assumptions: The seller holds RECEIPT_SIGNING_SECRET; whoever holds it can sign any receipt.

test_run.environment: node:22 container, network off, sources from git archive of 8743fd7
test_run.note: 1565 passed, 8 skipped, 3 failed of 1576: repo-identity needs git and two polyglot tests need python3 and cargo, none installed in the container

demonstrated_properties: signature over sha256(JSON of prevHash and payload)
per-signer hash chain via prevHash
not_demonstrated: that the served content is correct; a receipt attests what the seller signed
stable key ordering: JSON.stringify does not sort keys
a persistent signing key in the SDK seller and paywall, which generate an ephemeral key when none is supplied

claims.plain_claim: Receipt anchoring is opt-in and refuses to run unless the operator names a receipt_anchor deployment.
authority_assumptions: Any signer can append to any bucket; the program does not authenticate who anchors.

test_run.note: Devnet test evidence for the 2026-10-06 deployment is being recorded separately.

demonstrated_properties: server anchoring needs ANCHORING_ENABLED, RECEIPT_ANCHOR_PROGRAM_ID and ANCHORING_KEYPAIR_PATH (all unset by default)
liquefy-receipts 0.3.0 has no default program and throws RECEIPT_ANCHOR_UNAVAILABLE
deployed devnet bytes match the 2026-10-06 build output
not_demonstrated: that one anchor proves a single receipt: the program folds each 32-byte value into an hourly hash chain (root = sha256(prev_root || value)); inclusion needs the ordered list of anchors in that bucket
that the receipt hash is anchored: the server anchors the commit's payer commitment
a deployment configured as default in source (none, by design)
operational_limitations: If the anchoring client fails to build, the server keeps running with anchoring off.
The mainnet pilot receipt_anchor 6HSRGivdYR5D7yTDy1TFMCM8h3LzXxRtKU1RA3RnCMRN is closed; configs/mainnet.*.json still name it.
